title: Article 163 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor

content.overview: Article 163 provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions, except in so far as he is by or under the Constitution required to exercise his functions or any of them in his discretion. If any question arises whether a matter is or is not a matter as to which the Governor is required to act in his discretion, the decision of the Governor in his discretion is final, and the validity of anything done by the Governor shall not be called in question on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in his discretion. The question whether any, and if so what, advice was tendered by Ministers to the Governor shall not be inquired into in any court.
content.glance: CoM with CM aids and advises Governor, except where Constitution requires discretionary action. Governor’s decision on discretion is final. Advice not justiciable.
content.study:
Article 163 is the State counterpart of Article 74, with an important difference: it expressly contemplates areas where the Governor is required to act in his discretion. The scope of discretion is limited to what the Constitution requires (e.g. certain functions under Arts 200, 356-related contexts, and other express provisions); it is not a general reserve of independent power.

Examination: aid and advice as the rule; constitutional discretion as the exception; finality of Governor’s decision on whether discretion applies; non-justiciability of advice content; contrast Art 74 (no general discretion clause).

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Council of Ministers with CM at the head to aid and advise the Governor.
2. Exception: where the Constitution requires the Governor to act in his discretion.
3. Whether a matter is discretionary: Governor’s decision in his discretion is final; validity not open to challenge on that ground.
4. Advice content not open to court inquiry.
